topics.intent: Choose an agent-facing browser integration and distinguish Playwright CLI, Playwright MCP, Playwright Test, and codegen.
topics.distinctFromExisting: The 2026-10-22 MCP vs Chrome DevTools MCP article compares two MCP servers. This guide covers Microsoft's separate coding-agent CLI, command naming, installation, session state, and when MCP fits the runtime. It does not repeat the previous MCP-server comparison or Browser Use vs Playwright product comparison.

demandSignals.signal: The thread discusses CLI vs MCP and attaching an agent to an already-running end-to-end test. One reply describes trouble with the debug=cli session closing before attach. This indicates a concrete setup/debugging question; the post is an anecdotal discussion, not a prevalence measure.

A current discussion describes confusion over repeated page snapshots, context use, and choosing browser tools for interactive agent tasks versus tests. Treat the author's account as an anecdote; do not reuse its unsupported numeric/token claims.
Current official Playwright materials now provide a dedicated coding-agent CLI guide and distinguish CLI use from MCP use, showing an active product surface readers need to understand.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: The current installation guide requires Node.js 20 or newer. It documents npx playwright cli when the project already has Playwright installed, and npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest for the global playwright-cli executable.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Official installation guide checked 2026-10-23; page crawl displayed as three weeks earlier.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: The agent-facing Playwright CLI is a separate package/command surface from Playwright Test and codegen; current official setup documents @playwright/cli, playwright-cli, and npx playwright cli.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Official documentation checked 2026-10-23. Commands and installation requirements can change; verify the version in the project.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: CLI suits terminal coding-agent workflows; MCP is exposed through MCP hosts and can fit agent loops that use its session model. This is a task-fit recommendation, not a benchmark winner.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Interpretation based on official product descriptions; no performance or token comparison was run.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: CLI browser state is held in memory by default for a session and can be persisted; named sessions are documented.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Current repository documentation checked 2026-10-23; confirm behavior for the installed CLI release.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: MCP isolated sessions discard state when closed and support configured initial state/persistent user-data options; saved authentication state can carry sensitive cookies and headers.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Official documentation checked 2026-10-23; follow organization rules for credentials and profile access.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: The Playwright Test CLI debugger can pause a test for attachment through playwright-cli, according to current release notes.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Version-dependent feature; only use if the installed Playwright version documents it.

editorialLimits: No comparative task run or token benchmark was performed.
Reddit content is user-generated anecdote and not a measure of broad demand, reliability, or current tool performance.
The article gives no claim that CLI universally replaces MCP or Playwright Test.

topics.intent: Capture, select, inspect, troubleshoot, and safely share Playwright trace artifacts for browser-agent or test failures.
topics.distinctFromExisting: This is an operational failure-analysis guide about trace artifacts and their handling. It is not an MCP comparison or a generic browser-agent tool comparison.

demandSignals.type: official issue demonstrating report/trace debugging demand
demandSignals.signal: A Playwright issue reports a trace link selecting the first run rather than the selected retry in a multi-result HTML report. The issue was closed and linked to another issue/fix; it is a version-specific case and not evidence of a current general bug.

An open issue catalogs agent-oriented trace inspection and debugging primitives, including command-line trace analysis, as capabilities requested for browser-agent workflows. This is one project's feature request, not a market-size measure.

demandSignals.type: official issue demonstrating trace viewer troubleshooting questions
demandSignals.signal: A specific report describes a large trace that failed to open. It supports including a careful troubleshooting branch, not asserting a universal size limit or that the issue affects current users generally.

demandSignals.type: official current documentation and release surface
demandSignals.signal: Current official docs cover trace recording, viewer workflows, CI retry configuration, and opening saved archives; current release notes additionally document CLI trace analysis for agents.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: The Trace Viewer inspects recorded Playwright traces; saved files can be opened through npx playwright show-trace or trace.playwright.dev. The hosted viewer loads the trace in-browser and does not transmit trace data externally.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Official docs checked 2026-10-23. The privacy statement applies to trace loading by this viewer, not to public issue attachments or the file's storage/sharing.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: Playwright Test supports trace modes including on-first-retry, on-all-retries, retain-on-failure, on, and off; CI guidance recommends first-retry tracing, while full tracing can be expensive.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Current official docs checked 2026-10-23; exact defaults depend on the repository's config and installed version.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: The viewer exposes action sequence/timing, snapshots, logs, source, network, console, and error details; these are investigation evidence rather than a causal explanation of backend behavior.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Feature description from current official docs; the causal interpretation is editorial guidance.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: Saved authentication state can include sensitive cookies and headers that could impersonate a test account and should not be committed.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Direct warning in current Playwright auth documentation. Trace archives are separately advised for review because page snapshots and screenshots can contain private content.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: Issue 41281 reported a wrong trace link for a selected retry in a Playwright HTML report; issue 39845 reported a trace loading problem involving a large trace.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Specific historical issue reports, not generalized current defects or known product limits.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: Issue 38207 concerned browser local-network permission behavior for a remote trace URL in Chrome versions around 142, and is historical.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: Used only to contextualize a troubleshooting anecdote; the article does not present it as a current general restriction.

technicalClaimProvenance.claim: The Playwright v1.59 release notes introduce the agent trace-analysis CLI commands. browserContext.tracing records browser operations and network activity but excludes Playwright Test assertions; Test-runner configuration includes those assertions in a fuller failure trace.
technicalClaimProvenance.scope: The current official release notes group these commands under v1.59. Use npx playwright trace commands only with Playwright v1.59 or newer; the official API explicitly recommends Test-runner tracing when debugging assertions.

editorialLimits: No test suite, browser agent, or trace archive was executed or captured for this article.
Example config is documentation-derived and not tested in this repository.
Issue reports are version-specific and do not establish prevalence or present-day impact.
Trace content sensitivity varies by the page and data captured; inspect artifacts before sharing.
